CORE 1 CANONICAL REASONING SYSTEM

Build the Force-and-Momentum Reasoning System Before Transfer

Never start with a formula name. Start by choosing the body or system, identify interactions and state, build the representation, then select the governing physical invariant law.

1
CHOOSE
Which body or system is tracked? Define the closed boundary.
2
REPRESENT
FBD, interaction map, momentum state, motion graph, or system boundary.
3
CONNECT
Newton I / ΣF=ma / Δp/Δt / Newton III / momentum conservation.
4
EXECUTE + CHECK
Keep signs, units, bodies, and system membership explicit. Test limiting cases.
NLM-01 Pillar P1

Motion is not force

Constant velocity can coexist with zero net force
📖 Physical Story • What is Happening?

Newton I links change of velocity to net external force. Motion itself does not require a sustaining net force. A crate sliding at constant velocity on a frictionless surface has zero net force acting upon it.

Decisive Key Idea: If velocity is constant in an inertial frame, acceleration is zero (a = 0) and therefore the net external force is zero (Sigma F_net = 0).
🎨 Staged Conceptual Illustration
⚙️ How It Works (Step-by-Step Method)
  1. Choose the body and ask whether its velocity is changing.
  2. Draw all external forces acting on that body.
  3. Add them vectorially before discussing motion.
  4. Check: zero net force means constant velocity, including rest.
📝 Worked Example

A crate moves right at 3 m/s3\text{ m/s}3 m/s while 60 N60\text{ N}60 N right and 60 N60\text{ N}60 N left act on it. Fnet=0F_{\text{net}} = 0Fnet​=0, so a=0a = 0a=0; it continues at constant velocity indefinitely.

🎯 Guided Try

Prompt: A puck glides at constant velocity on an ideal frictionless surface. What horizontal net force is required?

Guide: Name the body/system -> draw the representation -> state the law before calculating.
Show Solution
Answer: 0 N0\text{ N}0 N. Zero net force is required to sustain constant velocity.
🔄 Faded Perturbation Try

Change one feature of the worked example (direction, mass, force, time, or system boundary). Which parts of the reasoning remain valid and which must change?

⚠️ Watch Out Trap

A moving object does not automatically need a forward net force.

Connected Core 2 Practice Items:
NLM-02 Pillar P1

Choose the body before drawing forces

Interactions become forces only after the body is chosen
📖 Physical Story • What is Happening?

A free-body diagram is a diagram of one chosen body. First identify what interacts with it; then draw only the forces acting on that body.

Decisive Key Idea: The phrase 'force on X by Y' prevents body confusion and Newton-III mistakes.
🎨 Staged Conceptual Illustration
⚙️ How It Works (Step-by-Step Method)
  1. Circle the body/system being analysed.
  2. List interacting bodies: Earth, surface, rope, hand, etc.
  3. Convert each interaction into one force arrow on the chosen body.
  4. Do not include forces the chosen body exerts on something else.
📝 Worked Example

For a book on a table, the book FBD contains Earth-on-book weight and table-on-book normal. The book-on-table force belongs to the table FBD.

🎯 Guided Try

Prompt: A crate is pushed by a worker while sliding on a floor. Name three possible external interactions on the crate.

Guide: Name the body/system -> draw the representation -> state the law before calculating.
Show Solution
Answer: Worker-crate contact push, Earth-crate gravity, floor-crate contact reaction and friction.
🔄 Faded Perturbation Try

Change one feature of the worked example (direction, mass, force, time, or system boundary). Which parts of the reasoning remain valid and which must change?

⚠️ Watch Out Trap

An interaction pair is not automatically two arrows on one FBD.

Connected Core 2 Practice Items:
NLM-03 Pillar P2

Net force is a vector sum

Balanced forces and no forces are different statements
📖 Physical Story • What is Happening?

Newton II uses the net external force, not whichever force is easiest to notice. Balanced forces can be nonzero individually while yielding zero acceleration.

Decisive Key Idea: Choose a positive axis, assign signs to force components, and sum them: ΣFx=max\Sigma F_x = m a_xΣFx​=max​ and ΣFy=may\Sigma F_y = m a_yΣFy​=may​.
🎨 Staged Conceptual Illustration
⚙️ How It Works (Step-by-Step Method)
  1. Choose +x and +y coordinate directions.
  2. Resolve forces into components when needed.
  3. Compute ΣFx\Sigma F_xΣFx​ and ΣFy\Sigma F_yΣFy​.
  4. Only then infer acceleration components.
📝 Worked Example

A cart has 25 N25\text{ N}25 N right and 10 N10\text{ N}10 N left. With right positive, Fnet,x=25−10=15 NF_{\text{net},x} = 25 - 10 = 15\text{ N}Fnet,x​=25−10=15 N right.

🎯 Guided Try

Prompt: A box has 30 N right and 30 N left. What is its horizontal acceleration?

Guide: Name the body/system -> draw the representation -> state the law before calculating.
Show Solution
Answer: 0 m/s20\text{ m/s}^20 m/s2, regardless of its current velocity.
🔄 Faded Perturbation Try

Change one feature of the worked example (direction, mass, force, time, or system boundary). Which parts of the reasoning remain valid and which must change?

⚠️ Watch Out Trap

Do not confuse 'F_net = 0' with 'there are no forces.'

Connected Core 2 Practice Items:
NLM-04 Pillar P2

Newton II and scaling

Acceleration responds to net force and mass together
📖 Physical Story • What is Happening?

For a chosen body of constant mass, Fnet=maF_{\text{net}} = maFnet​=ma. At fixed mass, aaa scales with net force; at fixed force, aaa scales inversely with mass.

Decisive Key Idea: For changes in both force and mass, compare ratios before substituting numbers: a2a1=(F2F1)(m1m2)\frac{a_2}{a_1} = \left(\frac{F_2}{F_1}\right)\left(\frac{m_1}{m_2}\right)a1​a2​​=(F1​F2​​)(m2​m1​​).
🎨 Staged Conceptual Illustration
⚙️ How It Works (Step-by-Step Method)
  1. Write a1=F1/m1a_1 = F_1 / m_1a1​=F1​/m1​ and a2=F2/m2a_2 = F_2 / m_2a2​=F2​/m2​.
  2. Form the ratio a2/a1=(F2/F1)(m1/m2)a_2 / a_1 = (F_2/F_1)(m_1/m_2)a2​/a1​=(F2​/F1​)(m1​/m2​).
  3. Keep direction from the signed net force.
  4. Check units: 1 N=1 kg⋅m/s21\text{ N} = 1\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m/s}^21 N=1 kg⋅m/s2.
📝 Worked Example

If force halves while mass doubles, aaa becomes (1/2)(1/2)=1/4(1/2)(1/2) = 1/4(1/2)(1/2)=1/4 of its original value.

🎯 Guided Try

Prompt: A 40 N net force accelerates 5 kg. What is a?

Guide: Name the body/system -> draw the representation -> state the law before calculating.
Show Solution
Answer: a=40/5=8 m/s2a = 40 / 5 = 8\text{ m/s}^2a=40/5=8 m/s2.
🔄 Faded Perturbation Try

Change one feature of the worked example (direction, mass, force, time, or system boundary). Which parts of the reasoning remain valid and which must change?

⚠️ Watch Out Trap

'Half the force means half the acceleration' is true only if mass is unchanged.

Connected Core 2 Practice Items:
NLM-05 Pillar P4

Stopping force needs two models

Kinematics supplies acceleration; Newton II supplies force
📖 Physical Story • What is Happening?

Stopping-over-distance problems often require a kinematics step before a force step. Do not jump directly from distance to force.

Decisive Key Idea: For constant stopping acceleration, find aaa from v2=u2+2asv^2 = u^2 + 2asv2=u2+2as, then use Fnet=maF_{\text{net}} = maFnet​=ma; find time separately if requested via v=u+atv = u + atv=u+at.
🎨 Staged Conceptual Illustration
⚙️ How It Works (Step-by-Step Method)
  1. Write the motion state: u,v=0,su, v=0, su,v=0,s.
  2. Use v2=u2+2asv^2 = u^2 + 2asv2=u2+2as to find acceleration aaa.
  3. Use F=maF = maF=ma with proper sign and direction.
  4. If time is needed, use v=u+atv = u + atv=u+at after aaa is known.
📝 Worked Example

A 0.020 kg0.020\text{ kg}0.020 kg pellet at 100 m/s100\text{ m/s}100 m/s stops uniformly in 0.10 m0.10\text{ m}0.10 m. a=(0−1002)/(2imes0.10)=−50,000 m/s2a = (0 - 100^2)/(2 imes 0.10) = -50,000\text{ m/s}^2a=(0−1002)/(2imes0.10)=−50,000 m/s2, so F=0.020(−50000)=−1000 NF = 0.020(-50000) = -1000\text{ N}F=0.020(−50000)=−1000 N.

🎯 Guided Try

Prompt: If the same pellet stops over twice the distance, what happens to |a| and |F|?

Guide: Name the body/system -> draw the representation -> state the law before calculating.
Show Solution
Answer: Both ∣a∣|a|∣a∣ and ∣F∣|F|∣F∣ halve.

Change one feature of the worked example (direction, mass, force, time, or system boundary). Which parts of the reasoning remain valid and which must change?

⚠️ Watch Out Trap

Do not mix the kinematic distance relation with Newton II as though they were one formula.

NLM-06 Pillar P3

Momentum is a signed state

Momentum carries the direction of velocity
📖 Physical Story • What is Happening?

Momentum is p⃗=mv⃗\vec{p} = m\vec{v}p​=mv. In one dimension its sign follows velocity. A change in direction can make Δp\Delta pΔp much larger than a simple speed difference.

Decisive Key Idea: Always write signed initial and final momenta explicitly: pi=mvip_i = m v_ipi​=mvi​, pf=mvfp_f = m v_fpf​=mvf​, then Δp=pf−pi\Delta p = p_f - p_iΔp=pf​−pi​.
🎨 Staged Conceptual Illustration
⚙️ How It Works (Step-by-Step Method)
  1. Choose a positive direction.
  2. Write signed velocities (+v or -v).
  3. Convert to signed momenta.
  4. Subtract final minus initial: Δp=pf−pi\Delta p = p_f - p_iΔp=pf​−pi​.
📝 Worked Example

A 0.20 kg0.20\text{ kg}0.20 kg ball changes from +8 m/s+8\text{ m/s}+8 m/s to −6 m/s-6\text{ m/s}−6 m/s. Δp=0.20(−6)−0.20(8)=−1.2−1.6=−2.8 kg⋅m/s\Delta p = 0.20(-6) - 0.20(8) = -1.2 - 1.6 = -2.8\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m/s}Δp=0.20(−6)−0.20(8)=−1.2−1.6=−2.8 kg⋅m/s.

🎯 Guided Try

Prompt: At fixed mass, what is the shape of a p-v graph?

Guide: Name the body/system -> draw the representation -> state the law before calculating.
Show Solution
Answer: A straight line through the origin; slope = mass.
🔄 Faded Perturbation Try

Change one feature of the worked example (direction, mass, force, time, or system boundary). Which parts of the reasoning remain valid and which must change?

⚠️ Watch Out Trap

Do not discard signs when a body rebounds.

Connected Core 2 Practice Items:
NLM-07 Pillar P3

Impulse and average force

The same momentum change can be spread over more time
📖 Physical Story • What is Happening?

Average force measures how quickly momentum changes: Fˉ=ΔpΔt\bar{F} = \frac{\Delta p}{\Delta t}Fˉ=ΔtΔp​. Increasing stopping time reduces force magnitude for the same Δp\Delta pΔp.

Decisive Key Idea: This is the physics behind moving the hands backward while catching a ball, automotive crumple zones, and air bags.
🎨 Staged Conceptual Illustration
⚙️ How It Works (Step-by-Step Method)
  1. Find the signed Δp=mΔv\Delta p = m\Delta vΔp=mΔv.
  2. Identify the interaction duration Δt\Delta tΔt.
  3. Divide Δp\Delta pΔp by Δt\Delta tΔt.
  4. Check force direction against Δp\Delta pΔp, not against initial velocity alone.
📝 Worked Example

A 0.50 kg0.50\text{ kg}0.50 kg ball at +12 m/s+12\text{ m/s}+12 m/s stops in 0.30 s0.30\text{ s}0.30 s: Δp=−6 kg⋅m/s,Favg=−20 N\Delta p = -6\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m/s}, F_{\text{avg}} = -20\text{ N}Δp=−6 kg⋅m/s,Favg​=−20 N.

🎯 Guided Try

Prompt: If the same ball is stopped in twice the time, what happens to average force magnitude?

Guide: Name the body/system -> draw the representation -> state the law before calculating.
Show Solution
Answer: It halves.
🔄 Faded Perturbation Try

Change one feature of the worked example (direction, mass, force, time, or system boundary). Which parts of the reasoning remain valid and which must change?

⚠️ Watch Out Trap

Momentum and force are not the same physical quantity.

NLM-08 Pillar P1

Newton III pairs

Equal and opposite does not mean same body
📖 Physical Story • What is Happening?

A third-law pair belongs to the same interaction, has equal magnitude and opposite direction, and acts on different bodies: F⃗AB=−F⃗BA\vec{F}_{AB} = -\vec{F}_{BA}FAB​=−FBA​.

Decisive Key Idea: Use complete names: 'force on B by A' and 'force on A by B'. Because they act on different bodies, they never cancel on a single FBD.
🎨 Staged Conceptual Illustration
⚙️ How It Works (Step-by-Step Method)
  1. Name both interacting bodies.
  2. Write the two force names.
  3. Place each force on the correct body's FBD.
  4. Use Newton II separately to compare accelerations.
📝 Worked Example

Earth pulls an apple downward with the same force magnitude that the apple pulls Earth upward. Their accelerations differ because their masses differ.

🎯 Guided Try

Prompt: What is the third-law partner of the table-on-book normal force?

Guide: Name the body/system -> draw the representation -> state the law before calculating.
Show Solution
Answer: The book-on-table contact force.
🔄 Faded Perturbation Try

Change one feature of the worked example (direction, mass, force, time, or system boundary). Which parts of the reasoning remain valid and which must change?

⚠️ Watch Out Trap

Weight and normal on a resting book are balanced forces on one body, not a Newton-III pair.

Connected Core 2 Practice Items:
NLM-09 Pillar P3

Momentum conservation is a system statement

Choose the system and check external impulse first
📖 Physical Story • What is Happening?

Total momentum is conserved only for a chosen system when the relevant external impulse over the interaction is negligible.

Decisive Key Idea: The equation Pbefore,total=Pafter,totalP_{\text{before,total}} = P_{\text{after,total}}Pbefore,total​=Pafter,total​ comes after the system/interval check.
🎨 Staged Conceptual Illustration
⚙️ How It Works (Step-by-Step Method)
  1. Draw a system boundary.
  2. Choose a positive direction.
  3. List all system momenta before and after.
  4. Check external impulse; then equate totals if valid.
📝 Worked Example

Two skaters push apart from rest. For the two-skater system, initial total p=0p=0p=0, so their final momenta are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.

🎯 Guided Try

Prompt: A falling ball speeds up under gravity. Is the ball-only momentum conserved?

Guide: Name the body/system -> draw the representation -> state the law before calculating.
Show Solution
Answer: No; gravity gives the ball an external impulse.
🔄 Faded Perturbation Try

Change one feature of the worked example (direction, mass, force, time, or system boundary). Which parts of the reasoning remain valid and which must change?

⚠️ Watch Out Trap

Do not claim conservation from one object's momentum alone when an external force acts on it.

Connected Core 2 Practice Items:
NLM-10 Pillar P3

Recoil, rockets and exchanged momentum

Equal momentum can mean very different speeds
📖 Physical Story • What is Happening?

In recoil/explosion problems with negligible external impulse, momentum exchanged internally appears with opposite signs.

Decisive Key Idea: For equal momentum magnitude, speed is inversely proportional to mass (v∝1/mv \propto 1/mv∝1/m). Kinetic energy also scales inversely with mass (K∝1/mK \propto 1/mK∝1/m).
🎨 Staged Conceptual Illustration
⚙️ How It Works (Step-by-Step Method)
  1. Choose launcher+projectile (or rocket+exhaust) as the system.
  2. Set initial total momentum.
  3. Assign opposite signs after separation.
  4. Solve one object's speed from total momentum conservation.
📝 Worked Example

A 0.020 kg0.020\text{ kg}0.020 kg bullet leaves a 2.0 kg2.0\text{ kg}2.0 kg pistol at +150 m/s+150\text{ m/s}+150 m/s from rest. 0=(0.020)(150)+2.0v0 = (0.020)(150) + 2.0v0=(0.020)(150)+2.0v, so v=−1.5 m/sv = -1.5\text{ m/s}v=−1.5 m/s.

🎯 Guided Try

Prompt: Two rifles fire identical bullets with the same bullet momentum. Which rifle has larger recoil speed?

Guide: Name the body/system -> draw the representation -> state the law before calculating.
Show Solution
Answer: The lighter rifle.

Change one feature of the worked example (direction, mass, force, time, or system boundary). Which parts of the reasoning remain valid and which must change?

⚠️ Watch Out Trap

A lighter rifle recoils faster for the same bullet momentum, not with a larger recoil momentum.

NLM-11 Pillar P4

Read force from a motion graph

v-t slope -> acceleration -> force
📖 Physical Story • What is Happening?

A velocity-time graph gives acceleration from its slope. If friction is the only horizontal force, then Ffriction=maF_{\text{friction}} = maFfriction​=ma.

CORE 1B RECONSTRUCTION • UNASSISTED RETRIEVAL

Test conceptual retention of Newton's Laws and friction thresholds without looking back at the textbook. Reconstruct the Atwood invariant, the reaction cone, and resolve cognitive dissonance paradoxes.

Stage 1 • Cognitive Dissonance Retrieval Gates

CDP-01 Cognitive Dissonance Gate
Scenario: A 100 kg person stands on a spring bathroom scale in a freely falling elevator (cable snapped, air resistance negligible).
Dissonance Dilemma: What does the scale read? 100 kg, 980 N, or 0 N?
💡 Authentic Model Resolution

0 N (Apparent weightlessness). Both person and scale accelerate downward at g. No normal contact force is required to prevent relative penetration.

CDP-02 Cognitive Dissonance Gate
Scenario: A horse pulls a wagon with force F_hw = 500 N. By Newton's 3rd Law, the wagon pulls back on the horse with F_wh = 500 N. How can the wagon possibly accelerate forward if the backward pull equals the forward pull?
Dissonance Dilemma: Why do these equal and opposite forces not produce static equilibrium?
💡 Authentic Model Resolution

The forces act on DIFFERENT bodies. To determine wagon acceleration, inspect forces acting ON THE WAGON (forward pull from horse minus wheel friction). The backward pull acts ON THE HORSE, which the horse overcomes by pushing backward against the ground with its hooves.

CDP-03 Cognitive Dissonance Gate
Scenario: You apply a horizontal force of 20 N to a heavy 50 kg crate on a rough floor with static friction coefficient mu_s = 0.5. The crate remains at rest.
Dissonance Dilemma: Is the static friction force acting on the crate 245 N (mu_s * m * g) or 20 N?
💡 Authentic Model Resolution

Exactly 20 N. mu_s * N = 245 N is the MAXIMUM POSSIBLE static friction threshold. Static friction matches the applied driving force exactly up to that threshold to maintain Sigma F = 0.

CDP-04 Cognitive Dissonance Gate
Scenario: A block sits at rest on the bed of an accelerating truck. As the truck speeds up forward, the block also speeds up forward without slipping relative to the truck.
Dissonance Dilemma: Which direction does friction on the block act? Forward or backward?
💡 Authentic Model Resolution

FORWARD. The only horizontal force acting on the block is static friction from the truck bed. By Newton's 2nd Law, Sigma F = m*a_forward, so friction must point in the direction of acceleration (forward).

CDP-05 Cognitive Dissonance Gate
Scenario: A 0.20 kg ball strikes a wall at 8 m/s and rebounds at 6 m/s. A student computes Delta p = 0.20*(8 - 6) = 0.40 kg m/s.
Dissonance Dilemma: What fatal error was committed, and what is the true momentum change?
💡 Authentic Model Resolution

Momentum is a signed directional vector. With initial direction positive, p_i = +1.6 kg m/s and p_f = -1.2 kg m/s. Delta p = p_f - p_i = -1.2 - (+1.6) = -2.8 kg m/s. Rebound produces roughly double the momentum change.

CDP-06 Cognitive Dissonance Gate
Scenario: A 0.020 kg bullet is fired from a 2.0 kg rifle. Both acquire equal momentum magnitudes |p|. Does the shooter receive as much kinetic energy as the target?
Dissonance Dilemma: Why is the bullet deadly while the rifle recoil is merely uncomfortable?
💡 Authentic Model Resolution

Kinetic energy K = p^2 / (2m). Because momentum magnitude |p| is identical, kinetic energy is inversely proportional to mass. The bullet (100 times lighter) absorbs 100 times more kinetic energy than the rifle.

Stage 2 • Phenomenological Reconstruction Cycles

RECON-01

Coupled Multi-Body Acceleration in Atwood Machine

Standard Isolated Formulation:

Separate FBDs: m1*g - T = m1*a and T - m2*g = m2*a. Adding equations eliminates tension T: (m1 - m2)*g = (m1 + m2)*a => a = (m1 - m2)*g / (m1 + m2).

✨ Phenomenological Perspective: Whole-System Center-of-Mass Invariant

Conceptual Pivot: Treat the two masses and the string as an unrolled 1D continuous chain along the string coordinate.

Reconstructed Invariant Law: a=Net Driving ForceTotal Inertia=(m1−m2)gm1+m2a = \frac{\text{Net Driving Force}}{\text{Total Inertia}} = \frac{(m_1 - m_2)g}{m_1 + m_2}a=Total InertiaNet Driving Force​=m1​+m2​(m1​−m2​)g​
Limiting Boundary Invariants:
  • m1 = m2: a = 0, T = m1*g (System in neutral static equilibrium)
  • m1 >> m2: a -> g, T -> 2*m2*g (m1 in free fall, pulling negligible m2 upward)
  • m2 = 0: a = g, T = 0 (Free fall of m1 with disconnected string)
RECON-02

Inclined Plane Slip Threshold & Angle of Repose

Standard Isolated Formulation:

Project gravity: along plane F_parallel = mg*sin(theta), normal F_perp = mg*cos(theta). Normal force N = mg*cos(theta). Slip condition f_s <= mu_s * N => mg*sin(theta) <= mu_s * mg*cos(theta) => tan(theta) <= mu_s.

✨ Phenomenological Perspective: Contact Reaction Cone Invariant

Conceptual Pivot: Combine normal reaction N and friction force f into a single total contact force vector R = N + f. For static equilibrium, R must be strictly vertical and collinear with gravity mg.

Reconstructed Invariant Law: tan⁡θ≤μs  ⟺  θ≤λ=arctan⁡(μs)\tan\theta \le \mu_s \iff \theta \le \lambda = \arctan(\mu_s)tanθ≤μs​⟺θ≤λ=arctan(μs​)
Limiting Boundary Invariants:
  • mu_s -> 0 (perfectly smooth): theta_repose = 0 deg; block slides on any non-zero incline
  • mu_s -> infinity (glued/toothed): theta_repose = 90 deg; block never slides along surface
  • theta = 0 deg (flat plane): Driving force = 0, normal N = mg, friction f_s = 0
RECON-03

Stacked Two-Block Slip Threshold on Frictionless Table

Standard Isolated Formulation:

Block A (mass m1) rests on Block B (mass m2). Horizontal force F pulls B. Max friction on A is f_max = mu*m1*g, giving A max acceleration a_max = f_max / m1 = mu*g. For no relative slip, whole system must accelerate at <= mu*g, so F_max = (m1 + m2)*a_max = mu*(m1 + m2)*g.

✨ Phenomenological Perspective: Non-Inertial Frame & D'Alembert Pseudo Force

Conceptual Pivot: Ride in the accelerating frame of bottom block B with acceleration a. A fictitious pseudo force F_pseudo = m1*a pulls block A backward.

Reconstructed Invariant Law: Fmax⁡=(m1+m2)amax⁡=μ(m1+m2)gF_{\max} = (m_1 + m_2) a_{\max} = \mu (m_1 + m_2) gFmax​=(m1​+m2​)amax​=μ(m1​+m2​)g
Limiting Boundary Invariants:
  • mu -> 0: F_max = 0; any non-zero pull causes B to slide out instantly
  • m1 >> m2: F_max -> mu*m1*g; inertia dominated entirely by top block
RECON-04

Movable Pulley Kinematic Invariant & Mechanical Advantage

Standard Isolated Formulation:

String length L = 2*y_pulley + y_load. Differentiating twice: 2*a_pulley + a_load = 0 => a_load = -2*a_pulley. Balance of forces on massless pulley: 2*T - F = 0 => T = F/2.

✨ Phenomenological Perspective: Virtual Work & Energy Conservation Invariant

Conceptual Pivot: An ideal machine cannot create energy: Input Work = Output Work. F * Delta x_input = W_load * Delta y_load.

Reconstructed Invariant Law: Win=Wout  ⟹  F⋅(2Δy)=Wload⋅Δy  ⟹  F=Wload2W_{\text{in}} = W_{\text{out}} \implies F \cdot (2\Delta y) = W_{\text{load}} \cdot \Delta y \implies F = \frac{W_{\text{load}}}{2}Win​=Wout​⟹F⋅(2Δy)=Wload​⋅Δy⟹F=2Wload​​
Limiting Boundary Invariants:
  • Inextensible string: Work input = Work output (Efficiency = 100%)
  • Elastic / stretching string: Mechanical advantage unchanged, but stored elastic energy reduces instantaneous work output

PHYS-NLM-001 D1 Foundational APPLY
Cognitive Profile: RETRIEVEEXPLAIN
A trolley moves to the right along a smooth horizontal track, and its speed increases steadily from rest. Which statement about the net horizontal force acting on the trolley is necessarily true?
💡 Progressive Socratic Hints (3 Tiers) 3 Tiers Available
Hint Tier 1: What is the Key Physics?
The trolley is moving right and speeding up. What does that tell you about the direction of its acceleration?
Its acceleration points to the right, the same direction as the velocity while the speed increases.
Hint Tier 2: How Would You Represent It?
For one chosen trolley, what representation connects that acceleration to the forces acting on it?
Draw the trolley FBD and form the horizontal vector sum ΣFx\Sigma F_xΣFx​.
Hint Tier 3: What Would You Write First?
What law would you write first after determining the acceleration direction?
Write ΣFx=max\Sigma F_x = m a_xΣFx​=max​. Use the acceleration direction from H1 only after you have written the law.
📐 5-Step Mathematical Reasoning Ladder & Proof Formal Verification
1. Understand: The velocity magnitude is increasing to the right, so acceleration is rightward.
2. Represent: Use one trolley FBD and the horizontal axis.
3. Connect: Newton II requires ΣFx=max\Sigma F_x = m a_xΣFx​=max​.
4. Calculate: Since ax>0a_x > 0ax​>0, ΣFx>0\Sigma F_x > 0ΣFx​>0: the net horizontal force is rightward.
5. Interpret: A rightward net force is required; individual forces need not all point right.
Final Analytical Expression: The net horizontal force is strictly non-zero and points to the right.
Independent Physical Verification
Dimensional Formula: [M L T^-2]
Limiting Cases:
  • dv/dt = 0 (constant velocity): FnetF_{\text{net}}Fnet​ = 0
  • dv/dt < 0 (slowing down rightward): FnetF_{\text{net}}Fnet​ directed left
Alternative Method: A leftward net force would make a right-moving trolley slow down, not speed up.
Watch Out Trap: Do not infer force direction from velocity alone; use the change of velocity.
PHYS-NLM-002 D1 Foundational EXPLAIN
Cognitive Profile: RETRIEVE
A student standing on the ground pushes horizontally against a rigid vertical wall with a force of 120 N120\text{ N}120 N. What force does the wall exert on the student?
💡 Progressive Socratic Hints (3 Tiers) 3 Tiers Available
Hint Tier 1: What is the Key Physics?
The student and wall are one interaction pair. What does Newton III say about the two interaction forces?
They are equal in magnitude, opposite in direction, and act on different bodies.
Hint Tier 2: How Would You Represent It?
How would you label the pair so body ownership cannot be confused?
Use 'force on wall by student' and 'force on student by wall'.
Hint Tier 3: What Would You Write First?
If the student-on-wall force is +120 N, what relation would you write first for the wall-on-student force?
F_(student by wall) = -F_(wall by student).
📐 5-Step Mathematical Reasoning Ladder & Proof Formal Verification
1. Understand: This is one contact interaction between two bodies: student and wall.
2. Represent: Represent the pair on two different bodies with explicit vectors.
3. Connect: Newton III: F(on student by wall) = -F(on wall by student).
4. Calculate: Magnitude is therefore 120 N, opposite the push direction.
5. Interpret: The wall exerts 120 N horizontally on the student away from the wall.
Final Analytical Expression: Exactly 120 N120\text{ N}120 N directed horizontally away from the wall (opposite the push).
Independent Physical Verification
Dimensional Formula: [M L T^-2]
Limiting Cases:
  • F_push -> 0: F_reaction -> 0
  • Wall mass M -> infinity: F_reaction remains exactly 120 N
Alternative Method: The student acceleration depends on the net force on the student, not on 'cancelling' this pair.
Watch Out Trap: Do not put both third-law forces on the same FBD.

A cricket ball of mass m=0.40 kgm = 0.40\text{ kg}m=0.40 kg traveling horizontally at vi=15 m/sv_i = 15\text{ m/s}vi​=15 m/s is caught and brought to rest. Compare the magnitude of the average force exerted on the fielder's hands if the ball is stopped in Δt1=0.10 s\Delta t_1 = 0.10\text{ s}Δt1​=0.10 s versus cushioned over Δt2=0.30 s\Delta t_2 = 0.30\text{ s}Δt2​=0.30 s.
💡 Progressive Socratic Hints (3 Tiers) 3 Tiers Available
Hint Tier 1: What is the Key Physics?
The initial and final momenta are the same in both catches. What quantity changes between the two cases?
Only the stopping time changes; the momentum change is the same.
Hint Tier 2: How Would You Represent It?
Which state representation makes the sign and size of the momentum change explicit?
Write pip_ipi​ = m v_i, pfp_fpf​ = 0, then Δp\Delta pΔp = pfp_fpf​ - pip_ipi​ for each case.
Hint Tier 3: What Would You Write First?
What force relation would you write first once Δp\Delta pΔp is known?
FavgF_{\text{avg}}Favg​ = Δp\Delta pΔp / Δt\Delta tΔt.

1. Understand: Same Δp\Delta pΔp in both catches; only Δt\Delta tΔt differs.
2. Represent: Take motion as positive: pip_ipi​ = 0.40(15) = 6 kg m/s and pfp_fpf​ = 0.
3. Connect: Use Favg=ΔpΔtF_{\text{avg}} = \frac{\Delta p}{\Delta t}Favg​=ΔtΔp​ with Δp=−6 kg⋅m/s\Delta p = -6\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m/s}Δp=−6 kg⋅m/s.
4. Calculate: |F_1| = 6.0 / 0.10 = 60 N; |F_2| = 6.0 / 0.30 = 20 N.
5. Interpret: Tripling stopping time reduces average force magnitude to one-third.
Final Analytical Expression: 60 N in the 0.10 s catch versus 20 N in the 0.30 s catch (one-third the force).

Limiting Cases:
  • Δt\Delta tΔt -> 0 (infinitely stiff): FavgF_{\text{avg}}Favg​ -> infinity
  • Δt\Delta tΔt -> infinity: FavgF_{\text{avg}}Favg​ -> 0

PHYS-NLM-004 D1 Foundational EXPLAIN
Cognitive Profile: RETRIEVE
A passenger standing upright in an aisle of a city bus lurches forward when the driver brakes suddenly. Which statement explains this phenomenon correctly without inventing a fictitious forward force of inertia?
💡 Progressive Socratic Hints (3 Tiers) 3 Tiers Available
Hint Tier 1: What is the Key Physics?
Immediately before braking, what horizontal velocity does the passenger's upper body already have?
The forward velocity of the bus relative to the road.
Hint Tier 2: How Would You Represent It?
When the bus decelerates, what horizontal contact force acts on the passenger's shoes from the floor?
Backward static friction decelerating the feet.
Hint Tier 3: What Would You Write First?
What horizontal force acts on the upper body before it tilts or grips a handrail?
Essentially zero; by Newton I, it tends to continue forward at constant velocity.
📐 5-Step Mathematical Reasoning Ladder & Proof Formal Verification
1. Understand: The passenger initially shares the bus forward velocity.
2. Represent: Represent the bus as slowing beneath the passenger; avoid a fictitious forward force in an inertial-frame FBD.
3. Connect: Newton I explains persistence of velocity until external forces change it.
4. Calculate: Feet are decelerated by backward floor contact; the upper body continues forward briefly, producing the lurch.
5. Interpret: The forward lurch is an inertia effect, not evidence of a new forward force.
Final Analytical Expression: The passenger's body continues forward with its pre-braking velocity because no horizontal force acts on the upper torso until muscles or handrails intervene.
Independent Physical Verification
Dimensional Formula: [M L T^-2]
Limiting Cases:
  • Acceleration a_bus = 0: No lurch (velocity unchanged)
  • Floor perfectly frictionless: Feet also glide forward at constant pre-braking velocity
Alternative Method: The actual contact force during braking is backward on the passenger, not forward.
Watch Out Trap: Do not invent a forward force of inertia in an inertial frame.
PHYS-NLM-005 D2 Standard Olympiad MODEL
Cognitive Profile: REPRESENTAPPLY
Inside a passenger train moving along a straight horizontal track with constant forward acceleration a0a_0a0​, a seated passenger tosses a coin vertically upward. Relative to the passenger, where does the coin land?
💡 Progressive Socratic Hints (3 Tiers) 3 Tiers Available
Hint Tier 1: What is the Key Physics?
While the coin is airborne, does it automatically share the train's continuing forward acceleration?
No; in flight, no horizontal force acts on the coin, so its horizontal velocity remains constant.
Hint Tier 2: How Would You Represent It?
During the flight time Δt\Delta tΔt, which covers a greater horizontal distance: the coin or the accelerating train?
The train, because its horizontal speed steadily increases while the coin's horizontal speed is fixed.
Hint Tier 3: What Would You Write First?
What coordinate difference x_train - x_coin develops over time Δt\Delta tΔt?
Δx\Delta xΔx = 1/2 a0a_0a0​ (Δt\Delta tΔt)^2 > 0 (train advances ahead of the coin).
📐 5-Step Mathematical Reasoning Ladder & Proof Formal Verification
1. Understand: The coin is launched vertically with horizontal velocity v0v_0v0​ equal to the train's instantaneous velocity at launch.
2. Represent: In the ground frame, coin executes projectile motion with vxv_xvx​ = v0v_0v0​ = const, while train position is x_train = v0v_0v0​ t + 1/2 a0a_0a0​ t^2.
3. Connect: Newton I governs horizontal motion of coin (ΣFx=0  ⟹  ax=0\Sigma F_x = 0 \implies a_x = 0ΣFx​=0⟹ax​=0).
4. Calculate: Relative horizontal position: x_coin,rel = x_coin - x_train = -1/2 a0a_0a0​ t^2 < 0.
5. Interpret: Because Δx\Delta xΔx < 0, the coin lands behind the passenger.
Final Analytical Expression: Strictly behind the passenger's hand.
Independent Physical Verification
Dimensional Formula: [M L T^-2]
Limiting Cases:
  • a0a_0a0​ = 0: Lands in hand
  • a0a_0a0​ < 0 (braking): Lands in front of hand
Alternative Method: In the accelerating frame of the train, an apparent backward pseudo force F_pseudo = -m a0a_0a0​ deflects the coin backward.
Watch Out Trap: Do not assume airborne objects maintain the acceleration of their launch vehicle.
PHYS-NLM-006 D1 Foundational RETRIEVE
A hockey puck slides across a perfectly smooth, ideal frictionless horizontal ice rink with constant velocity v⃗=4.0 m/si^\vec{v} = 4.0\text{ m/s}\hat{i}v=4.0 m/si^. What horizontal force is required to keep the puck moving at this constant velocity?
💡 Progressive Socratic Hints (3 Tiers) 3 Tiers Available
Hint Tier 1: What is the Key Physics?
The velocity of the puck is constant. What does Newton I say about constant velocity?
Constant velocity means acceleration is zero, which means net force is zero.
Hint Tier 2: How Would You Represent It?
What vertical forces act on the puck, and do they balance?
Gravity downward and normal upward balance completely: N = mg.
Hint Tier 3: What Would You Write First?
What horizontal force is required to keep an object moving at constant velocity on a frictionless surface?
Zero Newtons.
📐 5-Step Mathematical Reasoning Ladder & Proof Formal Verification
1. Understand: The puck moves at constant velocity on a frictionless horizontal plane.
2. Represent: One-body FBD has downward mg and upward normal N. No horizontal interaction exists.
3. Connect: Newton I: ΣF=0\Sigma F = 0ΣF=0 when velocity is constant in an inertial frame.
4. Calculate: ΣFx=0  ⟹  Fx=0 N\Sigma F_x = 0 \implies F_x = 0\text{ N}ΣFx​=0⟹Fx​=0 N.
5. Interpret: Motion itself does not require a sustaining force; force is required only to change velocity.
Final Analytical Expression: Exactly 0 N.
Independent Physical Verification
Dimensional Formula: [M L T^-2]
Limiting Cases:
  • Friction mu = 0: F_applied = 0
  • Friction mu > 0: F_applied = mu mg to maintain constant velocity
Alternative Method: By work-energy theorem, W_net = Delta K = 0; since displacement > 0, FnetF_{\text{net}}Fnet​ must be 0.
Watch Out Trap: Do not assume that moving objects automatically require a forward driving force.
PHYS-NLM-007 D3 Hard Olympiad MODEL
Cognitive Profile: REPRESENTAPPLY
A chemical rocket drifts at constant velocity in deep interstellar space far from any celestial gravitational fields. When its engine fires, it ejects hot exhaust gases backward at high speed. Explain why the rocket accelerates forward.
💡 Progressive Socratic Hints (3 Tiers) 3 Tiers Available
Hint Tier 1: What is the Key Physics?
Which two parts exchange momentum during the short ejection event?
Rocket and exhaust.
Hint Tier 2: How Would You Represent It?
What is the net external impulse acting on the rocket+exhaust system in deep space?
Zero, because there are no external gravitational or contact forces.
Hint Tier 3: What Would You Write First?
If the exhaust acquires backward momentum -Δp\Delta pΔp, what must the rocket acquire to keep total momentum constant?
+Δp\Delta pΔp (forward momentum).
📐 5-Step Mathematical Reasoning Ladder & Proof Formal Verification
1. Understand: The rocket and its fuel form an isolated multi-body system in deep space.
2. Represent: System boundary encloses rocket body and ejected exhaust gas.
3. Connect: System momentum conservation: ΔPsystem=0  ⟹  Δprocket+Δpexhaust=0\Delta P_{\text{system}} = 0 \implies \Delta p_{\text{rocket}} + \Delta p_{\text{exhaust}} = 0ΔPsystem​=0⟹Δprocket​+Δpexhaust​=0.
4. Calculate: Δprocket=−Δpexhaust>0\Delta p_{\text{rocket}} = -\Delta p_{\text{exhaust}} > 0Δprocket​=−Δpexhaust​>0.
5. Interpret: The rocket accelerates forward as a direct consequence of ejecting mass backward.
Final Analytical Expression: Backward momentum of ejected exhaust gases must be balanced by forward momentum of the rocket, conserving total system momentum (Delta P_total = 0).
Independent Physical Verification
Dimensional Formula: [M L T^-2]
Limiting Cases:
  • Exhaust ejection velocity v_rel = 0: Thrust = 0
  • Mass ejection rate dm/dt -> 0: Thrust = 0
Alternative Method: By Newton III, nozzle walls exert a backward force on the gas; the expanding gas exerts an equal forward thrust on the nozzle.
Watch Out Trap: Rockets do not need an atmosphere to push against; they push against their own expelled propellant.
PHYS-NLM-008 D2 Standard Olympiad JUSTIFY
Cognitive Profile: EXPLAINAPPLY
A road tanker carrying water is filled to three-quarters of its capacity and travels along a straight level road. When the driver applies the brakes suddenly, in which direction does the water surge inside the tank?
💡 Progressive Socratic Hints (3 Tiers) 3 Tiers Available
Hint Tier 1: What is the Key Physics?
Before braking, what velocity does the water already have relative to the road?
Approximately the tanker's forward velocity.
Hint Tier 2: How Would You Represent It?
When the tanker brakes, the tank walls decelerate. What horizontal force immediately decelerates the bulk water?
Only pressure forces once the water collides with the front bulkhead.
Hint Tier 3: What Would You Write First?
By Newton's First Law, what does the water tend to do while the tanker slows down beneath it?
It tends to maintain its forward speed, piling up toward the front of the tank.
📐 5-Step Mathematical Reasoning Ladder & Proof Formal Verification
1. Understand: The water initially shares the tanker's forward velocity.
2. Represent: In ground frame, the tanker decelerates (a_tank < 0) while bulk fluid continues at speed v0v_0v0​.
3. Connect: Newton I: mass tends to persist in uniform motion until external forces act.
4. Calculate: Relative displacement Delta x_water = x_water - x_tank > 0.
5. Interpret: Water surges forward toward the front bulkhead until pressure gradients balance deceleration.
Final Analytical Expression: The water surges forward toward the front of the tanker.
Independent Physical Verification
Dimensional Formula: [M L T^-2]
Limiting Cases:
  • Tanker acceleration a = 0: Water surface remains horizontal
  • Tanker accelerating forward (a > 0): Water surges backward toward rear
Alternative Method: In the tanker's decelerating frame, a forward pseudo force F_pseudo = -m a_tank tilts the effective gravity forward.
Watch Out Trap: Do not assume liquids behave differently from solids regarding Newton's First Law.
PHYS-NLM-009 D2 Standard Olympiad RETRIEVE
Three solid blocks AAA, BBB, and CCC of identical exterior shape and dimensions have masses mA=1.0 kgm_A = 1.0\text{ kg}mA​=1.0 kg, mB=3.0 kgm_B = 3.0\text{ kg}mB​=3.0 kg, and mC=5.0 kgm_C = 5.0\text{ kg}mC​=5.0 kg respectively. Rank the blocks in order of increasing translational inertia.
💡 Progressive Socratic Hints (3 Tiers) 3 Tiers Available
Hint Tier 1: What is the Key Physics?
What property measures resistance to a change in velocity in translational motion?
Mass.
Hint Tier 2: How Would You Represent It?
Do the exterior dimensions or geometric volume dictate inertia when masses are known?
No; mass alone determines translational inertia.
Hint Tier 3: What Would You Write First?
How do the three given masses compare in numerical magnitude?
1 kg < 3 kg < 5 kg.
📐 5-Step Mathematical Reasoning Ladder & Proof Formal Verification
1. Understand: Three bodies with identical geometry have different masses: 1 kg, 3 kg, 5 kg.
2. Represent: State the mass values along a 1D scalar scale.
3. Connect: Inertia scales directly with mass m.
4. Calculate: m_A (1 kg) < m_B (3 kg) < m_C (5 kg).
5. Interpret: Inertia ranking is strictly 5 kg > 3 kg > 1 kg (A < B < C).
Final Analytical Expression: A < B < C (1 kg < 3 kg < 5 kg).
Independent Physical Verification
Dimensional Formula: [M L T^-2]
Limiting Cases:
  • m -> 0: Inertia -> 0 (infinite acceleration for any non-zero force)
  • m -> infinity: Inertia -> infinity (zero acceleration)
Alternative Method: Accelerating 5 kg at 1 m/s^2 requires 5 N; accelerating 1 kg requires only 1 N.
Watch Out Trap: Do not confuse mass with volume or weight.
PHYS-NLM-010 D2 Standard Olympiad JUSTIFY
Cognitive Profile: EXPLAINAPPLY
A textbook question describes solid spheres resting on the floor of a train that brakes suddenly and claims the spheres 'roll forward'. Under the strict, literal idealization of a 'smooth' (frictionless) floor, which conclusion is physically valid?
💡 Progressive Socratic Hints (3 Tiers) 3 Tiers Available
Hint Tier 1: What is the Key Physics?
If the floor is truly frictionless, what horizontal contact force and rolling torque can it exert on a ball?
Zero horizontal force and zero torque.
Hint Tier 2: How Would You Represent It?
What forces appear on the FBD of the ball on an ideal smooth surface?
Vertical normal force N and vertical gravitational force mg only.
Hint Tier 3: What Would You Write First?
Can an object undergo angular acceleration about its center of mass without net torque?
No; tau = I alpha = 0 implies alpha = 0 (no rolling).
📐 5-Step Mathematical Reasoning Ladder & Proof Formal Verification
1. Understand: The question tests whether rolling motion can occur on an ideal frictionless floor.
2. Represent: Draw FBD of sphere: downward mg at COM, upward normal N at contact point. Zero horizontal force.
3. Connect: Rotational dynamics requires net torque tau = I alpha to initiate rolling.
4. Calculate: Torque about COM: tau = r x F_horizontal = r(0) = 0 => alpha = 0.
5. Interpret: Rolling is not justified by the literal smooth-floor model; the sphere translates without rolling.
Final Analytical Expression: On a truly smooth floor, only normal force and gravity act; without horizontal friction there is zero torque about the center of mass, so the spheres slide forward without rolling.
Independent Physical Verification
Dimensional Formula: [M L T^-2]
Limiting Cases:
  • Friction coefficient mu = 0: Pure sliding, zero rotation
  • Friction coefficient mu >> 0: Immediate pure rolling
Alternative Method: On an icy surface, a bowling ball skids forward without spinning until friction engages.
Watch Out Trap: Do not accept informal claims of rolling without checking the physical source of torque.
PHYS-NLM-011 D3 Hard Olympiad APPLY
Cognitive Profile: RETRIEVEEXPLAIN
Two rifles of masses M1=3.0 kgM_1 = 3.0\text{ kg}M1​=3.0 kg and M2=6.0 kgM_2 = 6.0\text{ kg}M2​=6.0 kg fire identical bullets with the same forward muzzle momentum pbullet=12 kg⋅m/sp_{\text{bullet}} = 12\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m/s}pbullet​=12 kg⋅m/s. Compare their recoil momenta and recoil speeds.
💡 Progressive Socratic Hints (3 Tiers) 3 Tiers Available
Hint Tier 1: What is the Key Physics?
For rifle+bullet systems initially at rest, what must the rifle momentum do when the bullet gets forward momentum?
Rifle momentum must be equal in magnitude and opposite in direction to conserve total p.
Hint Tier 2: How Would You Represent It?
How does recoil velocity relate to momentum and mass for each rifle?
v = p / M.
Hint Tier 3: What Would You Write First?
For equal momentum p = 12 kg m/s, how do the recoil speeds of 3 kg and 6 kg compare?
v_1 = 12/3 = 4 m/s; v_2 = 12/6 = 2 m/s (lighter rifle has twice the speed).
📐 5-Step Mathematical Reasoning Ladder & Proof Formal Verification
1. Understand: Two rifles of different masses fire bullets with identical momentum p.
2. Represent: Write momentum equations: p_bullet = +p, p_rifle = -p for both systems.
3. Connect: Momentum conservation P_tot = 0 => |p_recoil| = |p_bullet| = 12 kg m/s.
4. Calculate: Speed: v1 = 12 / 3.0 = 4.0 m/s; v2 = 12 / 6.0 = 2.0 m/s => v1 = 2 v2.
5. Interpret: Equal recoil momentum; lighter rifle has twice the recoil speed.
Final Analytical Expression: Both rifles have identical recoil momentum magnitude (12 kg m/s), but the lighter rifle has twice the recoil speed (4.0 m/s vs 2.0 m/s).
Independent Physical Verification
Dimensional Formula: [M L T^-2]
Limiting Cases:
  • M_rifle -> infinity: v_recoil -> 0, p_recoil = 12 kg m/s
  • M_rifle = M_bullet: v_recoil = v_bullet
Alternative Method: Lighter rifle has half the mass, so under the same internal impulse it acquires twice the acceleration.
Watch Out Trap: Equal momentum does not mean equal recoil speed or equal recoil energy.
PHYS-NLM-012 D2 Standard Olympiad APPLY
Cognitive Profile: RETRIEVEEXPLAIN
A horse pulls a cart along a level horizontal road at constant speed. The horse exerts a forward horizontal pull of 500 N500\text{ N}500 N on the cart. What is the total backward resistive force acting on the cart?

Hint Tier 1: What is the Key Physics?
The cart moves at constant velocity. What does that say about its acceleration and net horizontal force?
Acceleration is zero, so the net horizontal force must be zero.
Hint Tier 2: How Would You Represent It?
What horizontal forces act on the cart FBD?
Forward pull from the horse (500 N) and backward resistive friction/drag.

If FnetF_{\text{net}}Fnet​ = FpullF_{\text{pull}}Fpull​ - FresistF_{\text{resist}}Fresist​ = 0, what is FresistF_{\text{resist}}Fresist​?
FresistF_{\text{resist}}Fresist​ = 500 N.

1. Understand: The cart moves horizontally at constant speed under a 500 N forward pull.
2. Represent: Draw cart FBD: FpullF_{\text{pull}}Fpull​ = +500 N right, FresistF_{\text{resist}}Fresist​ left.
3. Connect: Newton II: ΣFx=max=0\Sigma F_x = m a_x = 0ΣFx​=max​=0 (since v=const  ⟹  a=0v = \text{const} \implies a = 0v=const⟹a=0).
4. Calculate: 500 - FresistF_{\text{resist}}Fresist​ = 0 => FresistF_{\text{resist}}Fresist​ = 500 N backward.

  • Resistance = 0 (ideal ice): Cart accelerates forward under any non-zero pull

PHYS-NLM-013 D3 Hard Olympiad JUSTIFY
Cognitive Profile: EXPLAINAPPLY
A tennis ball of mass mmm is dropped from a cliff. As it falls, its downward speed and momentum increase continuously. Can we claim that momentum is conserved for the ball-only system?
💡 Progressive Socratic Hints (3 Tiers) 3 Tiers Available
Hint Tier 1: What is the Key Physics?
What external force acts on the ball-only system during the fall?
Gravity from the Earth.
Hint Tier 2: How Would You Represent It?
What is required for a chosen system to conserve total momentum?
The net external impulse over the interaction must be zero.
Hint Tier 3: What Would You Write First?
Can a single body under an unbalanced external force conserve momentum?
No; Δp\Delta pΔp = FextF_{\text{ext}}Fext​ Δt\Delta tΔt != 0.
📐 5-Step Mathematical Reasoning Ladder & Proof Formal Verification
1. Understand: The ball accelerates downward under Earth's gravity.
2. Represent: Draw system boundary tightly around the ball alone. Gravity arrow crosses the boundary from outside.
3. Connect: Momentum theorem: dPsystemdt=ΣFext\frac{dP_{\text{system}}}{dt} = \Sigma F_{\text{ext}}dtdPsystem​​=ΣFext​. Here ΣFext=mg≠0\Sigma F_{\text{ext}} = mg \neq 0ΣFext​=mg=0.
4. Calculate: Δp=mgΔt>0\Delta p = mg \Delta t > 0Δp=mgΔt>0 (downward momentum increases).
5. Interpret: Momentum is NOT conserved for the ball-only system because gravity is external.
Final Analytical Expression: No, because an external force (gravity from the Earth) exerts an external downward impulse J = FextF_{\text{ext}}Fext​ Δt\Delta tΔt across the system boundary.
Independent Physical Verification
Dimensional Formula: [M L T^-2]
Limiting Cases:
  • g -> 0 (deep space): Ball momentum is strictly conserved
  • System = Ball + Earth: Total momentum is strictly conserved
Alternative Method: Earth accelerates upward by an undetectable amount m_ball g / M_Earth, conserving total momentum.
Watch Out Trap: Never assert momentum conservation without checking the system boundary for external forces.

Its velocity-time graph shows a linear decline from v0=80 m/sv_0 = 80\text{ m/s}v0​=80 m/s to rest in t=8.0 st = 8.0\text{ s}t=8.0 s. What physical quantity does the slope of a velocity-time graph represent?

What is the slope of the graph from (0 s, 80 m/s) to (8 s, 0 m/s)?

An object of mass mmm accelerates at aaa under a net horizontal force FFF. If the net force is halved (F′=F/2F' = F/2F′=F/2) while the mass of the object is doubled (m′=2mm' = 2mm′=2m), what is the new acceleration a′a'a′?

Hint Tier 1: What is the Key Physics?
How does acceleration depend on net force at fixed mass?
Directly proportional: a proportional to F.
Hint Tier 2: How Would You Represent It?
How does acceleration depend on mass at fixed force?
Inversely proportional: a proportional to 1/m.
Hint Tier 3: What Would You Write First?
Combine both scaling factors into the ratio a'/a.
a'/a = (F'/F) * (m/m') = (1/2) * (1/2) = 1/4.
📐 5-Step Mathematical Reasoning Ladder & Proof Formal Verification
1. Understand: Initial state: a = F/m. Final state: F' = F/2, m' = 2m.
2. Represent: Set up state scaling table: State 1 (F, m, a) -> State 2 (F/2, 2m, a').
3. Connect: Newton II: a = FnetF_{\text{net}}Fnet​ / m.
4. Calculate: a' = (F/2)/(2m) = (1/4)(F/m) = a/4.
5. Interpret: The new acceleration is one-fourth of the original acceleration (a/4).
Final Analytical Expression: a' = a/4.
Independent Physical Verification
Dimensional Formula: [M L T^-2]
Limiting Cases:
  • Mass unchanged (m' = m): a' = a/2
  • Force unchanged (F' = F): a' = a/2
Alternative Method: Take numbers: F = 20 N, m = 2 kg => a = 10 m/s^2. New: F = 10 N, m = 4 kg => a' = 2.5 m/s^2 = 10/4.

PHYS-NLM-016 D3 Hard Olympiad APPLY

Two ice skaters of masses m1=50 kgm_1 = 50\text{ kg}m1​=50 kg and m2=75 kgm_2 = 75\text{ kg}m2​=75 kg stand facing each other at rest on a frictionless frozen pond. They push apart, and skater 1 moves to the left at speed v1=3.0 m/sv_1 = 3.0\text{ m/s}v1​=3.0 m/s. What is the velocity of skater 2?

Hint Tier 1: What is the Key Physics?
For the two-skater system initially at rest, what is the total momentum before they push?
Zero: P_initial = 0.
Hint Tier 2: How Would You Represent It?
What external horizontal force acts on the two skaters on frictionless ice?
Zero; push forces between them are strictly internal.
Hint Tier 3: What Would You Write First?
If skater 1 has momentum (50 kg)(-3.0 m/s) = -150 kg m/s, what must skater 2 have?
+150 kg m/s to keep total momentum zero. Then solve v_2 = 150 / 75.

3. Connect: Momentum conservation: P_initial = P_final => 0 = m1 v1 + m2 v2.

5. Interpret: Skater 2 moves to the right at 2.0 m/s.

PHYS-NLM-017 D3 Hard Olympiad EXPLAIN
Cognitive Profile: RETRIEVE
A garden lawn sprinkler features horizontal radial arms with nozzles bent tangentially. When water under pressure is ejected backward from the nozzles, the sprinkler arms begin to rotate in the opposite sense. Why does this rotation occur?
💡 Progressive Socratic Hints (3 Tiers) 3 Tiers Available
Hint Tier 1: What is the Key Physics?
Which two bodies interact at each nozzle tip?
The nozzle metal and the water stream.
Hint Tier 2: How Would You Represent It?
If the nozzle exerts a force on the water to deflect it tangentially backward, what does the water exert on the nozzle?
An equal and opposite tangential force forward.
Hint Tier 3: What Would You Write First?
Does that forward reaction force generate a torque about the central pivot?
Yes; torque tau = r * F_reaction spins the arms in the sense opposite to the water jets.
📐 5-Step Mathematical Reasoning Ladder & Proof Formal Verification
1. Understand: Water is forced tangentially out of nozzles; arms rotate opposite to the jets.
2. Represent: Draw nozzle arm: water force vector points backward, reaction vector on arm points forward.
3. Connect: Newton III: F_(arm by water) = -F_(water by arm).
4. Calculate: Torque tau = r * F_reaction > 0 opposite to water spray.
5. Interpret: Sprinkler rotates opposite to the water jets due to third-law contact reaction.
Final Analytical Expression: By Newton's Third Law, when nozzle walls push water backward, the ejected water exerts an equal and opposite forward reaction force on the nozzles, generating a driving torque.
Independent Physical Verification
Dimensional Formula: [M L T^-2]
Limiting Cases:
  • Nozzle angle = 0 (radial spray): Torque = 0 (no rotation)
  • Water mass flow rate -> 0: Torque -> 0
Alternative Method: Angular momentum conservation of the (Sprinkler + Water) system requires counter-rotation when water carries angular momentum away.
Watch Out Trap: Do not invoke air resistance; the sprinkler operates even more freely in a vacuum chamber.

a = (0 - 10000) / (2 * 0.10) = -50,000 m/s^2.

How do you find stopping force F and time t once a is known?

1. Understand: m = 0.020 kg, u = 100 m/s, v = 0, s = 0.10 m. Unknowns: FstopF_{\text{stop}}Fstop​ and t.
2. Represent: Kinematic 1D state line: u -> v=0 over distance s.
3. Connect: Kinematic relation v2=u2+2asv^2 = u^2 + 2asv2=u2+2as; Newton II F=maF = maF=ma; time relation v=u+atv = u + atv=u+at.
4. Calculate: a = -100^2 / 0.20 = -50,000 m/s^2; F = 0.020(-50000) = -1000 N; t = 100 / 50000 = 0.0020 s.
5. Interpret: Average stopping force is 1000 N opposite to motion; stopping time is 0.0020 s.
Final Analytical Expression: Average retarding force |F| = 1000 N; stopping duration t = 0.0020 s.
Independent Physical Verification
Dimensional Formula: [M L T^-2]
Limiting Cases:
  • s -> 0 (infinitely rigid barrier): F -> infinity, t -> 0
  • u -> 0: F = 0, t = 0
Alternative Method: Work-energy: W = F * s = Delta K => F(0.10) = 1/2(0.020)(100^2) = 100 J => F = 1000 N.
Watch Out Trap: Do not treat stopping distance and stopping time as interchangeable.
PHYS-NLM-019 D3 Hard Olympiad SYNTHESIZE
Cognitive Profile: MODELAPPLY
A constant horizontal force F=5.0 NF = 5.0\text{ N}F=5.0 N produces an acceleration a1=8.0 m/s2a_1 = 8.0\text{ m/s}^2a1​=8.0 m/s2 on mass m1m_1m1​, and an acceleration a2=24.0 m/s2a_2 = 24.0\text{ m/s}^2a2​=24.0 m/s2 on mass m2m_2m2​. How do you find the masses m1 and m2 from the given force and accelerations?
m1 = F / a1 = 5/8 kg; m2 = F / a2 = 5/24 kg.
Hint Tier 2: How Would You Represent It?
What is the total mass when they are tied together?
M_tot = m1 + m2 = 5/8 + 5/24 = 15/24 + 5/24 = 20/24 = 5/6 kg.
Hint Tier 3: What Would You Write First?
What is the acceleration under the same force F = 5.0 N?
a = F / M_tot = 5 / (5/6) = 6.0 m/s^2. Or use 1/a = 1/a1 + 1/a2.

1. Understand: Force F = 5 N accelerates m1 at 8 m/s^2 and m2 at 24 m/s^2; find acceleration of (m1 + m2).
2. Represent: Table of states: Case 1 (m1 = F/8), Case 2 (m2 = F/24), Combined (M = m1 + m2).
3. Connect: Newton II: a_combined = F / (m1 + m2) = 1 / (m1/F + m2/F) = 1 / (1/a1 + 1/a2).
4. Calculate: 1/a = 1/8 + 1/24 = 3/24 + 1/24 = 4/24 = 1/6 => a = 6.0 m/s^2.
5. Interpret: Combined mass accelerates at 6.0 m/s^2 (strictly less than either mass alone).
Final Analytical Expression: a_combined = 6.0 m/s^2.
Independent Physical Verification
Dimensional Formula: [M L T^-2]
Limiting Cases:
  • m2 -> 0 (a2 -> infinity): a_combined -> a1 = 8 m/s^2
  • m1 = m2 (a1 = a2 = a): a_combined = a/2
Alternative Method: Formula a_tot = (a1 * a2)/(a1 + a2) = (8 * 24) / 32 = 192 / 32 = 6.0 m/s^2.
Watch Out Trap: Do not average accelerations; mass adds linearly, so accelerations add harmonically.

In an ideal Atwood machine with a massless, frictionless pulley, two masses m1=3.0 kgm_1 = 3.0\text{ kg}m1​=3.0 kg and m2=2.0 kgm_2 = 2.0\text{ kg}m2​=2.0 kg are connected by a light, inextensible string. Taking g=9.8 m/s2g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2g=9.8 m/s2, determine the system acceleration aaa and the tension TTT in the string.
💡 Progressive Socratic Hints (3 Tiers) 3 Tiers Available
Hint Tier 1: What is the Key Physics?
Treat the Atwood machine as an unrolled 1D system. What is the net driving force?
Net driving force = (m1 - m2)g = (3.0 - 2.0)(9.8) = 9.8 N.
Hint Tier 2: How Would You Represent It?
What is the total system inertia being accelerated by that driving force?
Total inertia = m1 + m2 = 3.0 + 2.0 = 5.0 kg.
Hint Tier 3: What Would You Write First?
How do you evaluate acceleration a and string tension T?
a = 9.8 / 5.0 = 1.96 m/s^2; T = m2(g + a) = 2.0(9.8 + 1.96) = 23.52 N.
📐 5-Step Mathematical Reasoning Ladder & Proof Formal Verification
1. Understand: Two masses m1 = 3 kg and m2 = 2 kg are coupled by a light string over a frictionless pulley.
2. Represent: Draw individual FBDs: m1 has downward m1 g and upward T; m2 has downward m2 g and upward T.
3. Connect: Equations of motion: m1 g - T = m1 a; T - m2 g = m2 a.
4. Calculate: Add equations: (m1 - m2)g = (m1 + m2)a => a = (1.0)(9.8)/5.0 = 1.96 m/s^2. T = 2(3)(2)(9.8)/5 = 23.52 N.
5. Interpret: Acceleration is 1.96 m/s^2; tension is 23.52 N (less than m1 g = 29.4 N, greater than m2 g = 19.6 N).
Final Analytical Expression: a = 1.96 m/s^2; T = 23.52 N (the harmonic mean of gravitational weights).
Independent Physical Verification
Dimensional Formula: [M L T^-2]
Limiting Cases:
  • m1 = m2: a = 0, T = m1 g (neutral static equilibrium)
  • m2 -> 0: a -> g, T -> 0 (free fall of m1)
Alternative Method: Tension formula T = [2 m1 m2 / (m1 + m2)] g represents the harmonic mean of the two gravitational weights.
Watch Out Trap: Tension is NOT equal to (m1 + m2)g or (m1 - m2)g.
PHYS-NLM-022 D4 Achievers HOTS JUSTIFY
Cognitive Profile: EXPLAINAPPLY
A block of mass mmm rests on a rough ramp whose inclination angle θ\thetaθ can be varied. The coefficient of static friction is μs\mu_sμs​. Using the Contact Reaction Cone invariant, at what maximum angle θrepose\theta_{\text{repose}}θrepose​ can the ramp be tilted before the block slips down?
💡 Progressive Socratic Hints (3 Tiers) 3 Tiers Available
Hint Tier 1: What is the Key Physics?
Combine the normal reaction N and friction force f into a single total contact vector R.
R = N + f. For equilibrium, R must be vertical and collinear with gravity mg.
Hint Tier 2: How Would You Represent It?
What is the maximum angle λ\lambdaλ between contact reaction vector R and the surface normal?
tan(λ\lambdaλ) = f_max / N = (μs\mu_sμs​ N) / N = μs\mu_sμs​.
Hint Tier 3: What Would You Write First?
Since R is vertical, what is the geometric relationship between the incline angle θ\thetaθ and cone angle λ\lambdaλ?
θ\thetaθ = λ\lambdaλ, meaning slip occurs when tan(θ\thetaθ) > μs\mu_sμs​.
📐 5-Step Mathematical Reasoning Ladder & Proof Formal Verification
1. Understand: Find threshold angle θ\thetaθ before slip occurs on inclined plane with static friction μs\mu_sμs​.
2. Represent: Draw FBD with contact reaction cone: R = N + f, gravity mg downward.
3. Connect: Static equilibrium: R balances mg => R is vertical. Angle between R and normal is θ\thetaθ.
4. Calculate: At slip threshold: f_s = f_max = μs\mu_sμs​ N => tan(θ\thetaθ) = f_max / N = μs\mu_sμs​.
5. Interpret: Repose angle satisfies tan(theta_repose) = μs\mu_sμs​, completely independent of mass m.
Final Analytical Expression: tan(theta_repose) = μs\mu_sμs​ (independent of block mass m).
Independent Physical Verification
Dimensional Formula: [M L T^-2]
Limiting Cases:
  • μs\mu_sμs​ -> 0 (perfectly smooth): theta_repose = 0 deg (slides on any incline)
  • μs\mu_sμs​ -> infinity (toothed): theta_repose = 90 deg (never slides)
Alternative Method: Project forces along incline: mg sin(θ\thetaθ) <= μs\mu_sμs​ mg cos(θ\thetaθ) => tan(θ\thetaθ) <= μs\mu_sμs​.
Watch Out Trap: Angle of repose depends only on surface roughness μs\mu_sμs​, not on block weight.

What is the maximum force Fmax⁡F_{\max}Fmax​ that can be applied without block AAA slipping relative to block BBB? (Take g=9.8 m/s2g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2g=9.8 m/s2).

What is the only horizontal force that can accelerate top block A forward?
Static friction f_s from the top surface of block B.

What is the maximum horizontal acceleration that friction can impart to block A?
a_max = f_max / m1 = (μs\mu_sμs​ m1 g) / m1 = μs\mu_sμs​ g = 0.40(9.8) = 3.92 m/s^2.

If both blocks move together at a_max, what total horizontal force F_max must pull the composite mass (m1 + m2)?

2. Represent: Draw FBD for m1: forward friction f_s. For m2: forward pull F, backward friction f_s from m1.

5. Interpret: Maximum pull force without slip is exactly 19.6 N.

Dimensional Formula: [M L T^-2]

  • μs\mu_sμs​ -> 0: F_max = 0 (slips under any non-zero force)
  • m1 >> m2: F_max -> μs\mu_sμs​ m1 g
Alternative Method: In accelerated frame of B, pseudo force on A is m1 a; slip occurs when m1 a > μs\mu_sμs​ m1 g => a > μs\mu_sμs​ g.

A conical pendulum consists of a small bob of mass m=0.50 kgm = 0.50\text{ kg}m=0.50 kg suspended by a light string of length L=1.0 mL = 1.0\text{ m}L=1.0 m revolving at constant speed in a horizontal circle of radius rrr, with the string making a constant angle θ=60∘\theta = 60^\circθ=60∘ to the vertical. Taking g=9.8 m/s2g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2g=9.8 m/s2, what are the string tension TTT and the net horizontal centripetal force FnetF_{\text{net}}Fnet​?
💡 Progressive Socratic Hints (3 Tiers) 3 Tiers Available
Hint Tier 1: What is the Key Physics?
What forces act on the bob, and along which axes do they resolve?
Tension T along the string and gravity mg downward. Resolve T into horizontal T sin(θ\thetaθ) and vertical T cos(θ\thetaθ).
Hint Tier 2: How Would You Represent It?
Is there any vertical acceleration for the bob revolving in a horizontal circle?
No; aya_yay​ = 0, so T cos(θ\thetaθ) = mg => T = mg / cos(θ\thetaθ).
Hint Tier 3: What Would You Write First?
What provides the net centripetal force directed toward the center of the horizontal circle?
The horizontal component of tension: FnetF_{\text{net}}Fnet​ = T sin(θ\thetaθ) = mg tan(θ\thetaθ).
📐 5-Step Mathematical Reasoning Ladder & Proof Formal Verification
1. Understand: Bob of mass m = 0.50 kg revolves at angle θ\thetaθ = 60 deg to vertical; find T and horizontal FnetF_{\text{net}}Fnet​.
2. Represent: Draw FBD of bob: downward mg, tension T at angle θ\thetaθ to vertical.
3. Connect: Vertical equilibrium: ΣFy=Tcos⁡θ−mg=0\Sigma F_y = T \cos\theta - mg = 0ΣFy​=Tcosθ−mg=0. Horizontal dynamics: ΣFx=Tsin⁡θ=Fnet\Sigma F_x = T \sin\theta = F_{\text{net}}ΣFx​=Tsinθ=Fnet​.
4. Calculate: T = 0.50(9.8) / cos(60 deg) = 4.90 / 0.50 = 9.80 N. FnetF_{\text{net}}Fnet​ = 9.80 sin(60 deg) = 9.80(sqrt(3)/2) = 4.90 sqrt(3) approx 8.49 N.
5. Interpret: Tension is 9.80 N; net horizontal centripetal force is 8.49 N.
Final Analytical Expression: Tension T = mg / cos(60 deg) = 9.80 N; Net horizontal force FnetF_{\text{net}}Fnet​ = mg tan(60 deg) = 4.90 sqrt(3) N approx 8.49 N.
Independent Physical Verification
Dimensional Formula: [M L T^-2]
Limiting Cases:
  • θ\thetaθ -> 0 (rest at bottom): T -> mg = 4.90 N, FnetF_{\text{net}}Fnet​ -> 0
  • θ\thetaθ -> 90 deg (horizontal string): T -> infinity, FnetF_{\text{net}}Fnet​ -> infinity
Alternative Method: Vector triangle of forces: T^2 = (mg)^2 + (FnetF_{\text{net}}Fnet​)^2 => 9.80^2 = 4.90^2 + 8.487^2 => 96.04 = 24.01 + 72.03 = 96.04.
Watch Out Trap: Do not assume net force is zero merely because speed is constant in uniform circular motion.
